title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This is a short scratch computation in item 3), sub-part 2°). It is written on the back of a typed name label (L.-B. Coupiac, allocataire de recherches) and sits between pages of an administrative circular. The problem is to find an elliptic element of SL2(Z) of trace 1, i.e. a+d=1, so d=1-a. Since ad-bc=1, the characteristic polynomial is X^2 - X + 1, so the eigenvalues are primitive 6th roots of unity. The element has order 6 in SL2(Z) and order 3 in PSL2(Z). Grothendieck takes the simplest choice a=0, d=1, which forces bc=-1, and takes b=1, c=-1. This gives rho = (0 1; -1 1), acting by z -> 1/(1-z). Its fixed point in the upper half-plane solves z^2 - z + 1 = 0, so z = 1/2 + i*sqrt(3)/2 = exp(2i*pi/6) = e^{i*pi/3}. This is the elliptic point of order 3 of the modular curve (the j=0 point). Presumably sub-part 1°) treated trace 0, i.e. the order-4 element S with fixed point i. The context is the 'Teichmülleries': torsion in the Teichmüller modular group Gamma_{1,1} = SL2(Z) and the special points of M_{1,1}, the base case of the Teichmüller tower studied in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error. rho^3 = -I, so rho has order 6 in SL2(Z). The fixed point is correct: 1 - e^{i*pi/3} = e^{-i*pi/3}, so 1/(1-z) = z.
The final '= [?]' is an unreadable symbol, perhaps a notation for the point (rho, j, or similar). Note that z = e^{i*pi/3} = -rho_Serre^2, where Serre writes rho = e^{2i*pi/3}.

ideas.what: Element of SL2(Z) of trace 1 (order 6) and its fixed point e^{i*pi/3} in the upper half-plane
ideas.modern_name: elliptic elements and elliptic points of order 3 of the modular group (j=0 point of M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Dedekind; textbook, e.g. Serre's Cours d'arithmétique)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the modular groups Gamma_{1,1}, Gamma_{0,4} and their torsion in general terms; this explicit computation is textbook material

deep.surprise_reason: A routine textbook computation of the order-3/6 torsion element of SL2(Z) and its fixed point. It is scratch work on administrative paper, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The top-left entry of the matrix is 0, written over a crossed-out character.
